To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a new estimator that uses machine learning to predict the outcomes and reduce the variance of the treatment effect estimator, and (2) the new estimator is robust and performs well in practice.

MLRATE is a robust, consistent, asymptotically normal estimator of the average treatment effect, and that in A/A tests on 48 common outcome metrics in Facebook experiments, MLRATE has over $70 \%$ lower variance than a difference-in-means baseline, and about $20\%$ lower than an univariate adjustment for pre-experiment outcome values.

(1) machine learning predictors of outcome can reduce estimator variance, even in the presence of uncorrelated noise; (2) the gains are large, and are robust to the presence of unobserved confounders; (3) the estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal, and (4) the estimator is easy to use, and is available in the open source R package mlrte
